questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanted to spend time somewhere I had never been before. It was important for me that the place I was going to was not differing too much from Denmark and that the spoken language was English. Being close to nature and having the opportunity to ski was important for me as well

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was kind of difficult to find information about courses etc. Also, there was a lot to do with Covid (study permit and so on) which was very confusing

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to swap one of my courses but weren't sure about a couple of things so I called the supervisor from Denmark and they were very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The options were limited due to Covid and if you applied you could be lucky to get a spot on campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Didn't use meal plans. I lived in a studio apartment and it had nothing in it when I arrived so I had to go buy pots, pans, plates, cutting boards, etc in the beginning.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Overall I think it was very nice to live on campus. However, I lived in a residence that had construction work in it and right beside it the whole semester. Also, the residences, in general, are kind of noisy. But if I had to go again I would still choose to live on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You were asked to make a list of 10 courses but I don't think the date for registering was very clear. Also, it is very hard to find information about the courses like exam form, time and place, etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't feel like there was that much help to get. I e-mailed KU a couple of times where I didn't get any answer.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Again the date confused me and the registration page broke down while I was doing it, so Without me knowing I had only registered for 3-4 courses and had to choose the last one between the few courses that were left.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just ask if anything confuses you and don't be afraid of calling the student service center I think they are very helpful!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two 100 level courses and two 200 level courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think it was pretty much the same

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Ling 101 - languages of the world
Soci 101 - Interaction and culture
Anth 217 - Culture and Communication 
crwr 213 - Introduction to creative writing for the new media

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I found Soci 101 really interesting and it was not that hard to understand the concepts.
I also liked Anth 217 but the professor was kind of all over the place

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was really surprised by the price of the housing

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is less expensive and groceries are more expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was limited because of Covid and opportunities to use badminton, basketball courts, etc closed during the exam period and there was a "clubs fair" when there were only 2 months left of the term.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Vancouver has so much to offer! Both on-campus (like museums, gardens, etc.) and in downtown, Kitsilano and North Van.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Whistler, Vancouver Island, Squamish - just all of the fun outdoor stuff to do in and around Vancouver

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Enroll in clubs and don't be afraid of talking or asking for help the first couple of weeks!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I feel like the Canadian culture reminds a lot about the Danish, so I didn't really face any challenges

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Canadians are super friendsly! I loved that.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Remember to spend time on fun things during the week even though you feel busy
2. take courses that sound interesting to you 
3. Take advantage of all of the things the city has to offer and enjoy your time here

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The workload is bigger than at UCPH but the level is not as high. There are weekly quizzes and assignments in many courses but it's not too bad. In some of my courses you got points for submitting (not taking into account if it was right or wrong)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying to live and establish an everyday life in a different culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Covid-19

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
